plan: Encapsulate state: Workspace deep-copies the input dict on construction and to_data() returns a deep copy, so callers can never alias internal state.

Single traversal primitive: a recursive pre-order generator over item lists feeds total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and the containment check, with kind-based dispatch (note vs reference vs container) at each visit.

Text semantics via two regexes: markers matched as \[\[\?(\w+)\]\] are collected for unresolved_markers and stripped from note text before words are counted with \b\w+\b; references contribute their declared word_count and unresolved list directly.
Outline: emit the workspace title, then recurse over items accumulating '  ' * depth + '<kind>: <title>' lines, depth starting at 1 for top-level items, joined with newlines for determinism.
Locate helper returns (parent item list, index, item) for any id via recursive search, giving move both the node and its removal site in one pass.

Move as validate-then-commit: check both ids are strings, resolve the item, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal maps to the root list, otherwise must be a section/group), reject self/descendant destinations using an identity-based subtree scan, and bounds-check an explicit index against the destination length — all before mutating; only then delete from the source list and append/insert into the destination, preserving the subtree object wholesale.
mechanisms: deep-copy boundary on construction and export
regex marker extraction and marker-stripped word counting
